ne56f57b73f1.s: Which Dutch factory was established in 1645?
ne56f57b73f1.x: Karaikal came in 1645, after Surat (1616) and before Chinsura (1653) and Nagapattinam (1658).

n3f34f641649.s: Which of the following English settlements on the Andhra coast is NOT correctly matched with its year?
n3f34f641649.x: Visakhapatnam came in 1682; Armagaon was the 1626 settlement.

n994e574c2e4.s: Mustafanagar, one of the Northern Circars granted to the French by Salabat Jang in 1753, is also known as:
n994e574c2e4.x: Mustafanagar is Kondapalli; Eluru, Rajahmundry and Chicacole were the other Circars granted.

n9979978a0ae.s: In which year did the Dutch capture Pondicherry?
n9979978a0ae.x: The Dutch captured Pondicherry in 1693; it was restored in 1697 (Ryswick).

new.s: The Dutch took Nagapattinam in 1658 from the:
new.x: Nagapattinam was taken by the Dutch from the Portuguese in 1658 and later became their chief factory.

new.s: Cochin, taken by the Dutch from the Portuguese in 1663, passed to the British in:
new.x: Cochin (Dutch from 1663) passed to the British in 1795; 1824 is the Anglo-Dutch Treaty.

new.s: Fort Geldria, the only Dutch fortification in India, stood at:
new.x: Fort Geldria at Pulicat was the Dutch's only fort in India; Bheemunipatnam has the Dutch cemetery.

new.s: Which place in Andhra Pradesh has a Dutch cemetery, a remain of the Dutch factory of 1641?
new.x: Bheemunipatnam (1641) is known for its Dutch cemetery.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Fort Geldria?
o: It was the only Dutch fortification in India
It was blown up by the British in 1804
new.x: Fort Geldria was at Pulicat, not Bheemunipatnam, which is known for its Dutch cemetery.

new.s: In which year did the Dutch set up their factory at Bheemunipatnam?
new.x: Bheemunipatnam was founded in 1641; Palakollu came in 1652, Pulicat in 1610, Machilipatnam in 1605.

new.s: Palakollu (Palicol), a Dutch factory of 1652, was a weaving centre of the:
new.x: Palakollu was a Godavari delta weaving centre; Nizampatnam (Petapuli) was the Krishna delta centre.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Dutch in Andhra:
1. Pulicat was the Dutch Coromandel headquarters till 1690.
2. Nizampatnam was the Dutch headquarters on the Coromandel coast.
3. Fort Geldria was built at Pulicat.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Pulicat with Fort Geldria was the HQ till 1690; Nizampatnam was only a Krishna delta weaving centre, not the HQ.

new.s: Pulicat under the Dutch was a hub of the:
new.x: Pulicat was a hub of the slave trade to Batavia, not of porcelain.

new.s: In the Dutch carrying trade, saltpetre came mainly from:
new.x: Saltpetre came from Bihar; pepper came from Malabar.

new.s: Under the Dutch, Koringa in Andhra was known for:
new.x: Koringa was a Dutch shipbuilding centre; jute was at Chittavalasa.

new.s: In the Battle of Bedara (1759), the English commander who defeated the Dutch was:
new.x: Francis Forde led the English at Bedara; J.B. Russell led the Dutch.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Bedara – ended Dutch ambitions in Malabar
new.x: Colachel (1741) was won by Marthanda Varma of Travancore; Bedara (1759) was English vs Dutch.

new.s: The Anglo-Dutch conferences that failed to end English-Dutch rivalry were held in:
new.x: The Anglo-Dutch conferences of 1613 and 1615 failed, adding to English rivalry.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a cause of the decline of the Dutch in India?
o: Their priority on Indian territory over the Indonesian spice monopoly
Loss of Andhra strongholds in the Anglo-French wars
new.x: The Dutch put the Indonesian spice monopoly first, not Indian territory.

new.s: Who reached Bantam in 1596, opening the Dutch route to Asia?
new.x: Cornelis de Houtman reached Bantam in 1596; Linschoten wrote the Itinerario.

new.s: The first Dutch factory in Bengal was at:
new.x: The Dutch first set up in Bengal at Pipali (1627), later Balasore; Chinsura came in 1653.

new.s: Bombay came to Charles II as the dowry of Catherine of Braganza in:
new.x: Bombay was dowry in 1661 and was leased to the Company in 1668.

new.s: Bombay replaced which place as the chief English settlement on the west coast?
new.x: Bombay replaced Surat, the early Western Presidency.

new.s: Sir Thomas Roe came to Jahangir's court in 1615 as the ambassador of:
new.x: James I sent both Hawkins and Roe to Jahangir.

new.s: Edward Terry at Jahangir's court was:
new.x: Edward Terry was Roe's chaplain; Hippon captained the Globe and Surman led the 1717 mission.

new.s: The Golden Farman of 1632 was issued by:
new.x: Abdullah Qutb Shah, Sultan of Golconda, issued the Golden Farman in 1632.

new.s: Under the Golden Farman, the English traded freely in Golconda ports for a yearly payment of:
new.x: The Golden Farman fixed 500 pagodas a year; Rs 3,000 and Rs 10,000 belong to the 1717 Farman.

new.s: Armagaon, the English settlement of 1626, is the present-day:
new.x: Armagaon is Dugarajapatnam in today's Tirupati district, 35 miles north of Pulicat.

new.s: The land for Madras was granted in 1639 by the Chandragiri ruler:
new.x: Venkatapati Raya III of Chandragiri gave the grant, with efforts of the Damerla brothers.

new.s: Fort St. George was completed on St George's Day, 23 April:
new.x: Begun in 1639-40, Fort St. George was completed on 23 April 1644.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the founding of Madras:
1. Francis Day founded it with Andrew Cogan.
2. The Damerla brothers helped obtain the grant.
3. Madras became India's first municipality in 1861.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Madras was founded in 1639 by Francis Day and Andrew Cogan with the Damerla brothers' help; it became a municipality in 1687 (Bhimili was Andhra's first in 1861).

new.s: The English East India Company's first voyage (1602) was led by:
new.x: James Lancaster led the first voyage in 1602 with £68,000 capital, setting up a factory at Bantam.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Charter of 1600?
o: It was granted by Elizabeth I
It gave a 15-year monopoly of East Indies trade
It gave territorial governance and legislative power
new.x: The 1600 Charter gave trading rights only, not territorial or legislative power (APPSC-GS 2024).

new.s: Child's War (1686-90) ended with the English East India Company:
o: pardoned on payment of a fine
new.x: Aurangzeb crushed the Company, which was pardoned on payment of a fine.

new.s: The early English settlements got silk and cotton piece-goods mainly from:
new.x: Silk and cotton piece-goods came from Bengal, not Gujarat.

new.s: Diamonds and rubies traded by the early English came from:
new.x: Diamonds and rubies came from Golconda; Bihar gave saltpetre and opium.

new.s: The English factories at Hariharpur and Balasore (1633) were on the coast of:
new.x: Hariharpur and Balasore (1633) were on the Odisha coast.

new.s: Under the Farman of 1717, all duties at Surat were dropped for a yearly payment of:
new.x: Surat duties went for Rs 10,000 a year; Bengal trade became duty-free for Rs 3,000.

new.s: Before founding Calcutta, Job Charnock was chief of the factory at:
new.x: Job Charnock, chief of the Qasim Bazar factory, chose Sutanuti and arrived in 1690.

new.s: Fort William, the nucleus of Calcutta, was built in:
new.x: Charnock arrived in 1690, the villages were bought in 1698 and Fort William came in 1700.

new.s: Which was the last European company to arrive in India?
new.x: The French East India Company (1664) was the last European company to arrive.

new.s: The charter of the French East India Company gave it a monopoly for:
new.x: The 1664 charter gave a 50-year monopoly in the Indian and Pacific Oceans.

new.s: In which year did the French settle at Yanam?
new.x: Yanam came in 1723, Mahe in 1725 and Karaikal in 1739.

new.s: Mahe, a French settlement of 1725, lies on the:
new.x: Mahe is on the Malabar coast; Chandernagore is in Bengal and Yanam in the Godavari delta.

new.s: Permission for the French settlement at Chandernagore (1673) was given by:
new.x: Shaista Khan gave permission in 1673; it was settled in 1690.

new.s: Pondicherry was restored to the French from the Dutch by the Treaty of:
new.x: The Treaty of Ryswick (1697) restored Pondicherry from the Dutch; Paris (1763) restored it from the British.

new.s: Sher Khan Lodi, who granted the land for Pondicherry in 1673, was a governor of:
new.x: Sher Khan Lodi was the Bijapur governor of Valikondapuram.

new.s: Which French governor obtained the right to mint rupees at Pondicherry in 1736?
new.x: Dumas (1735-41) got the right to mint rupees in 1736.

new.s: Who replaced Dupleix as French governor in 1754?
new.x: Godeheu replaced Dupleix in 1754 after the Treaty of Pondicherry.

new.s:
Arrange the following French governors in chronological order:
1. Dupleix
2. Francois Martin
3. Godeheu
4. Dumas
new.x: Francois Martin (died 1706), Dumas (1735-41), Dupleix (1742-54), Godeheu (1754).

new.s: Dupleix received a jagir at:
new.x: Dupleix got the jagir of Valapadu and was made Nawab south of the Krishna.

new.s: Dupleix was made Nawab of the Mughal territory south of the river:
new.x: The Deccan rulers made Dupleix Nawab of the Mughal territory south of the Krishna.

new.s: At Tumnapalem (1756), Bussy and Vijayaramaraju fought against:
new.x: Tumnapalem (1756) was Bussy and Vijayaramaraju against Jafar Ali; Bobbili (1757) was against Ranga Rao.

new.s: Who killed Vijayaramaraju after the Battle of Bobbili?
new.x: Tandra Papayya, Ranga Rao's brother-in-law, killed Vijayaramaraju.

new.s: Colonel Forde captured Machilipatnam from the French in:
new.x: Machilipatnam fell to Forde in 1759; the other Circars became British in 1768 and Guntur in 1788.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Yanam:
1. It was the only French territory in Andhra.
2. It stayed under French control until 1954.
3. It was founded by the French in 1739.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Yanam (1723) was the only French territory in Andhra, French until 1954; 1739 is Karaikal.

new.s: Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe and Yanam joined India de jure in:
new.x: They joined de facto in 1954 and de jure in 1962; Chandernagore joined in 1950.

new.s: Which of the following was NOT a French enclave left after the Treaty of Paris (1763)?
new.x: After 1763 the French kept only Pondicherry, Karaikal, Mahe, Yanam and Chandernagore; Machilipatnam had fallen to the British in 1759.
